column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
The entry places adat in the Majapahit Empire; the article does not mention Majapahit, so nothing was said of it. Left out the long list of other-language spellings.

Entry: commanded from about 457; article says 456/7 or around 458 for appointment: left as 'around 458' only for scholars' view. Entry has no birth date. Entry says 'domain of Soissons' held by Aegidius; article only says Gregory mentions Soissons held before Syagrius. Left out Wiomad story and Cologne/Trier details.

Entry says king from 590 and 'by marrying Theodelinda'; article: title in Nov 590, investiture May 591; chosen on her advice and married her afterwards. Both dates stated in the text as the article gives them; the marriage causality not stated.

Entry says ruled 1767-1795 from Maheshwar and Kashi Vishwanath 'in 1780'; article gives no date for the temple rebuilding, so none printed. Article's own 'Reign' section is about 1766-67. Heading 'In office' used since the guide forbids 'Reign' here only for non-monarchs; she was a queen but ruled de facto, so 'In office' is a deliberate choice; change to Reign if the editor prefers.

Entry says he ruled through nominal Walashma sultans; the article names only Umar Din as puppet sultan. Entry says jihad 1527-1543; article gives Imam of Adal 1527-1543 and invasion from 1529 (Shimbra Kure). Text does not state a start for the jihad. Article says 'Ahmad Gragn' conflation warning (Didier Morin) left out.

Entry says Abdallah 'unilaterally declared' independence on 6 July 1975; the article only says the islands became independent on that date. Text follows the article without the word 'unilaterally'. Article calls the 1978 coup leader nominal; entry says 'with mercenary help'.

Entry says eruption in 17th or 16th century BCE; article says 16th century BC in the lead and gives radiocarbon 1620-1530 BC. Dates printed as the article gives them; the 1620 figure is 17th century BCE so the two agree. Left out the path, pottery detail.
Article lead says the Seljuks captured Jerusalem in July 1099: an apparent slip (the body says Crusaders); not used. Entry says rule 1094-1101, matching.

Entry says it held towns in 2011-2012 and 2015-2016; article gives territorial peak 2015 and later decline, 2016 not stated. Left out the 'most radical branch' judgment, current leader, membership estimates.
Entry says Woolley excavated 'from 1936'; article says 1937-1939 and 1946-1949. Years left out. Left out DNA haplogroups and CTH texts.
Entry names ancient Cyme and a petrochemical complex; the article does not (it names Myrina, Gryneion, Aigai), so those were left out. Article has population 2022 only; kept as dated fact.
Entry says Constantius took Boulogne before Allectus murdered Carausius, as article. Article gives 'died c. 296 AD' and the Calleva site as archaeological suggestion.
Entry gives 28,800 years from the Sumerian King List; article agrees and also lists the other traditions. Left out the Pazuzu and Hurrian Alalu proposals.

Entry says Historia Brittonum made him 'a rival and successor of Vortigern'; article only says Vortigern ruled in fear of him (William of Malmesbury says he ruled after Vortigern). Wrote what the article says. Entry date '5th century'; no firm dates in text. Draft slightly long: check word count.
Entry: imprisoned 1499; article gives August 1499 and 32 months, consistent. Entry says Padua July 1509 matches. The article's 'Padua opened his way to the dogeship' is attributed in text.

Article gives birth as 1836 (lead) and 1833 (early years); entry says 1836; birth year left out. Entry 'Wizard of the Andes', article 'Andes Warlock': Spanish form used. Left out the article's garbled passage on beheading of captured Chileans and the present-day etnocacerista paragraph.
Entry: 'around 1787'; article says took power in 1787. Fine. Left out marriages, social organisation, laws on tombs.

Entry says Fronde exile; article says she fled Paris out of fear and stayed at Saint-Fargeau until 1657. Entry says she 'gave' the Dombes; article says she sold them. Wrote 'selling' per article; entry's word 'gave' for editor to review. The statement that Lauzun's arrest in 1671 was 'without an official reason' is paraphrased loosely and omitted.

Entry mentions the Negro Fort (1816) and Creek and Seminole communities; the article does not, so left out. Entry says the British used the river as the East/West Florida boundary in 1763; article gives no year, so none printed.

Entry says d. 497 BCE; article 497/496: death year left out. Entry says 'tyrant of Miletus ruling in place of Histiaeus'; article says appointed deputy/ruler. Article says 'Persian invasion of Greece in 490 BCE' and also, in the lead, 'two years after the defeat of the Ionians'; 490 used as in body. Mentions Greek Wikipedia-like lead claims about Hittites ignored.
Article says he was prime minister 1815-1818 and again from 21 Feb 1820 to 12 Dec 1821: consistent with entry. Left out Odessa Steps statement and plague dispute.

Article says dynasty ruled 189 BC to 12 AD; entry says c. 189 BCE to early 1st century CE. Article's own dates for Artaxias I are 190-159 BC and the founding is also given as 200 BC by D. M. Lang: I left Artaxias's own years out.
Article states the Livy 'three last straws'; wording hedged with 'is said to have counted'. Article says Caesar's last words contested. Entry and article agree on 44 BCE.

Entry says they separated from the Yanktonai Dakota; article says that was formerly believed and linguistic analysis shows they are coordinate with the Santee, Lakota and Yankton-Yanktonai. Also the article gives splitting from the Sioux 'prior to 1620' and 'in the 1500s'. Left the separation point out of the text.

Article inconsistent on exam start (1313 introduced; 1315 quota example); entry says 1315 restored: gave 1315 only for the appointments example. Skipped 'salary rice' decree attributed to Temur 1320 (looks like a slip).

Entry describes Azcapotzalco as Tepanec capital and 1428 Triple Alliance victory; the article holds little on the Tepanec period beyond one sentence (this is only its lead and section openings), so History is mostly earlier periods. Article's Culture mentions Moctezuma treasure legend: omitted.

Article: Hainaut count 1051-1070 as Baldwin I; entry says the succession war ended with Robert's victory at Cassel in 1071; article only says Arnulf III was killed at Cassel 1071. Wrote the article's version.

Entry says the strait links Bali Sea with Indian Ocean and 'long a route for trade and migration': latter not in article, not repeated. Article's geography list names the Bali Strait among Bali's own surrounding waters (a slip); omitted. Text is short of 260 words because the article is thin.

SKIPPED: article under about 250 words of substance (versions, a few covers, a list of languages) and adds little to the entry Article notes later changes to the text after Mussolini's rise (opening line changed from Compagni avanti alla riscossa to Avanti o popolo, alla riscossa) and covers by Pankrti 1984, KUD Idijoti 1986 and 1990; could be added by a later pass with another source.
Article gives Someshvara I as 1041-1068 and 1042-1068, capital 1050-1195: avoided his dates. Entry says capital from the mid-eleventh century: consistent.

Entry says the viceroy was defeated and captured; article says wounded, and Canterac's text mentions imprisonment and injury. Article is itself inconsistent on whether the Spanish defeat was a betrayal; attributed to Losada. Independence act dated 6 August 1825 and assembly 8 July 1825 per article.

Article says armistice discussed, final armistice reduced to 14 weeks. Article reports 2026 discovery of Dannebroge wreck: omitted. Nelson's telescope story told as 'is said' (article hedges only through its source).
Article's figure of 40,000 for the Achaemenid army is ambiguous (Cyrus's army?): left out.

SKIPPED: the saved article is about the Battle of Fontenoy of 11 May 1745 (War of the Austrian Succession), a different subject from the entry's 841 CE Carolingian battle Entry (841 CE, Lothair I against Louis the German and Charles the Bald) needs the article on the 841 battle; add to entries/more-mismatch.tsv.
Article says the battle was 'the second major encounter' and Chelmsford's column; entry says 'centre column': consistent.

Entry says the Japanese 31st Division was forced to retreat: consistent. 'Stalingrad of the East' label omitted. Garrison relief dates: article says relieved by mid-April, 18 April leading troops, 20 April handover.

Article says Frederick was marching from Como to Pavia; the entry says forces defeated: consistent. Article gives 'Frederick's capture of Rome 1167' and disease: I wrote 'disaster that struck his army at Rome in 1167'.
Article gives 'Stream Line Jane' operations starting 10 September; the lead says opened 10 September. Allied casualties in the later operations about 30 killed and 90 wounded.

Entry says Gnaeus was 'caught and executed soon afterwards'; article says cornered and killed at the Battle of Lauro: wrote 'cornered and killed'. Article's 30,000 dead / Caesar's 1,000 given as reported.
Entry says Manuel 'escaped and agreed a truce'; article says he fought out of the pass. Article states 'Manuel's death, empire drifted into anarchy': omitted.
Article title is Battle of Nahavand; spelled Nihavand/Nahawand there. 'Victory of Victories' not in article, not used. Article gives 642 (matches entry).

Article: independence declared 30 May, retroactive to 28 May; entry says declared 28 May. Date left out of text. Article says the battle 'prevented the complete destruction of the Armenian nation'; not used.

Dates: entry says c. 390 BCE or 387 by Greek reckoning; article says c. 387 most probable. I give no firm date in the text except a reference to modern view c. 387 BCE -- see checker; may remove. Cornell's first name not in article (fixed below if flagged).

Entry mentions Swiss regiments; not in article, not used. Article uses 'Battle of Berezina'. Entry says 'engineers built bridges under fire' - matches. Article says 'Overall approximately 40,000 saved'.
Entry says she 'refused British offers of a pension'; article does not say this, left out. Entry: 'a wife'; article: second wife / junior wife. Article gives birth 1820 and death 7 April 1879.

Entry says 'expulsion of some three million Germans'; article says about 3 million ethnic Germans and Hungarians (1945-47), and about 90% of Germans; I use the article's wording. Left out the December 2025 Slovak bill and other recent politics. Legal status 'ineffective since 31 Dec 1991' in Slovakia omitted.
Article inconsistent on the sale of Lübeck's share (stamps section says 1867, history says effective 1 January 1868, entry says 1868): I give 1 January 1868 only. 2020 population left out.

Article inconsistent on accession year (lead 1028, history 1027) and gives birth c. 1015 against the entry's c. 1017; no accession or birth year printed. Article calls him the last scion of Peter of Cantabria to rule; entry says last of male line of Astur-Leonese kings; neither stated.

Entry says Gian Galeazzo 'seized him by a ruse'; article says deposed on 6 May 1385: I say deposed. Entry says he ruled eastern half from 1354 (article: inherited with brothers 1354, Bergamo, Brescia, Cremona, Crema). Entry says 'governed from Milan': not stated in the article.
Entry says caravans were Tuareg and went to the Hausa lands, and that Bilma lay between Lake Chad and Libya; the article says only Azalai from Agadez and a Hausa minority: not stated by me.

Entry says death 967 or 972; article lead 972, Cosmas 967 questioned: no death year printed. Article says duke from 935, 'or 929 according to other sources' for the murder; I print 935 and the alternative for the murder only. Article's description of the war's start in 935 is garbled; I kept it as given.
Article says 1604 revision resulted in the 1604 Book; entry lists 1552, 1559, 1662 only: no conflict. Entry says 1549 'replaced the Latin services'; fine.

Entry says baptised around 870 and that he himself moved his seat to Prague Castle and built a church; article says baptised probably 883, and that the move to Hradčany was by the duke or more probably Spytihněv. I print 883 as 'probably' and the attribution as hedged; the entry's 870 and church are not printed. Entry's 'grandson Saint Wenceslas' is not in the article.

Article gives birth c. 841, entry c. 844: not printed. Article says Richard the Justiciar was Boso's brother; entry says Carolingian kings besieged 880-82: consistent. Entry says 'brother-in-law of Charles the Bald': matches.

SKIPPED: article under about 250 words of substance (a short history paragraph plus a list of rulers); adds little to the description Article: partitions 1398 and 1440, reunion 1420, sale to Prussia 2 December 1791, annexed 28 January 1792; entry says 1806 passed to Bavaria, not in article.
The article is about breechloaders in general, including artillery; I wrote about rifles and small arms. The Sokoto Caliphate and Maxim guns in the entry are not in the article and not mentioned.
Entry dates it c. 7th century BCE; article 7th-6th century BCE: only 'about the 7th to 6th century BCE' given, hedged. Entry says Ajatashatru of Kashi; article names Ajatashatru without Kashi.

Entry says it occupied the Zimbabwe plateau in 1890 and that First Chimurenga 1896-97 drew on Rozvi traditions; the article gives neither, so I leave them out. Article's reference to Pioneer Column is undated except by the 1890 medal note. Article places Maxim use in 'First Matabele War and Second Matabele War' without specifying which.

Entry says he crushed a Uyghur revolt in 546; article says a revolt of Tiele tribes, undated and disputed (Zizhi Tongjian 551; Cen Zhongmian earlier; Xue Zongzheng 550 or earlier); only the 546 tribute is dated in the article. I omit a year for the revolt. Article gives death 552 (AD).
Entry says he resigned in 1919 in protest; matches article. Article's claim that Cai 'established the Ministry of Education in 1927' omitted as unclear.
Caledon-style disagreements: none. Article says manuscripts span 6th-19th centuries; entry says mostly 10th-13th: text avoids a range. Khazar/Kievan letters left out.

SKIPPED: article has under 250 words of substance, and gives a length (642 km) that differs from the entry's 480 km (the article itself gives both) Article gives 642 km in the lead and about 480 km in Geography.

Article gives 2,560 km to San Juan Pueblo and use 1598-1882; entry says some 2,500 km to Santa Fe and 'nearly three centuries': length, terminus and span left out. Entry says Oñate's colonists in 1598; article says military scouts led by Oñate: text says the scouts. 'By 1000 CE' is the article's 'By 1000 AD'. Long lists of declared sites omitted.
No dates printed: entry gives trad. 808 BCE / 9th or 8th century, article says only 'before the first Olympiad'. Short article (566 words); text is near the lower limit.
Heading 'In office' used for the presidencies; 'Early life and background' for youth. No conflicts with entry.
Article says castle built 1177; entry says the same. Titanic, Troubles and notables left out.

Chronology disputed within the article (reign 7, 17 or 32 years; 568 battle thought unlikely; reign proposed 581-588); no reign length printed, Chronicle dates attributed. Entry's 592/593 agree with Chronicle. The 571 Bedcanford annal names Cuthwulf, not Ceawlin: only mentioned as 'towns won in 571', following the article's own sentence.

Entry says Spanish colonisation from 1668; article gives only 1521 (Magellan) and Spanish era 1521-1898: 1668 left out. Entry 'about 3,500 years ago' = article's c. 1500 BCE. Article itself gives two origin accounts (Philippines vs Sulawesi DNA); both told, attributed. Entry says 'largest ethnic group on Guam': not stated, left out.

Entry's Som Chand and 'first seat of the Chand dynasty' are not in the article; text follows the article (capital moved to Almora mid-16th century, consistent with entry's 16th century). Climate, transport, education left out.
Entry says she is created from the goddess's anger; the article gives eyebrows of Kaushiki / frown of Parvati: 'anger' not printed. Article has three origin stories; told as given.

Article contradicts itself on the abdication: lead and last abdication paragraph say 14 March 1849, but the 1848 paragraph says he abdicated on 19 April 1848 (the text says he fled in 1848 and abdicated for good 14 March 1849). Sequence in the article puts Austrian reoccupation in April 1849 after the 14 March 1849 abdication: text words this loosely ('regained Parma in April 1849, and abdicated ... 14 March 1849'), which keeps the article's own order problem; the editor may wish to reword. Entry: Lucca 1824-1847 agrees. Río de la Plata candidacy left out.

Only the lead and openings of sections given. Entry says he 'commanded imperial troops at Pavia'; article says he fought there: text says fought. Entry's Constable appointment not dated in lead beyond 1515: 'after 1515'. Children died young: omitted.
Article says Seraikella developed 'under the rule of Kalinga's Gajapati Rule' (garbled): left out. Article places Mayurbhanj in Odisha and Seraikela in Jharkhand, as the entry.

Article gives route as 1,170 miles (1,900 km) in lead and 1,880 km later: no distance printed. Pursued numbers: 800 (lead) vs about 750 (War section): text uses 750 only. Lead says Joseph succeeded 'in the early 1870s', the Leadership section says 1871.

Article gives two dates for the first chinampas (Culhuacan c. 1100 CE; earliest securely dated 1150-1350): only the second printed. The Nahuatl gloss differs inside the article ('in the fence of reeds' vs 'square made of canes'): the latter used.

Article contradicts itself on workers ('tens of thousands of former slaves' vs 'up to 20,000'): only the latter printed; entry says 'many thousands'. Entry dates c. 1805-1820 agree with article (commissioned 1805, completed 1820).
Entry says the system's Taira link and 'lingered formally' - consistent with article.
Article gives conflicting numbers for the force (Theopompus 800; 2600 'by 338 BC' under Alexander): none printed. Gaugamela in the entry is not discussed in the article.

Entry says the special position of the Catholic Church was removed in 1972; the article says the Fifth Amendment in 1973: no year printed. Article names the 1937 'plebiscite'; entry says referendum. Entry: 'approved on 1 July 1937' agrees; in force 29 December 1937 from article.

Entry dates c. 622; article reports scholars' dating disagreement (622 or shortly after, after 624, before 624): all attributed. Entry says 'attributed to Muhammad'; article says drafted by Muhammad per tradition. Told as tradition/scholarship.
Article calls the city Qift/Gebtu; desc says Coptos is the Greek name: consistent. Article date 'AD 292' used.

Article says 'in 1773' for the Corn Act 1772 (13 Geo. 3); I wrote 'Corn Act 1772' without the year of passing conflict. Article gives 1 February 1849 as the end of gradual reductions; left out. 'Reception and legacy' used as the closing heading for a legal work. Article: 'imported grain 2% dependence in 1830s ... 45% in 1880s'; I wrote 'of consumption', which the article does not say: see edit.
SKIPPED: article has under about 250 words of substance (about 330 words, much of it the lede, the legacy street names and a short biography the description already covers)

Desc: ruled 534-560, with Cerdic taking the Isle of Wight; article gives reign 534-560 but I printed none of the reign dates, and Dumville's alternative 554-581 left out because it conflicts with desc. Isle of Wight not in the article. Article says 'son (or in some sources grandson)': both told. Film depiction left out.

Article gives Elsloo 882 etc.; omitted. Article says Edward the Confessor abolished heregeld in 1051; omitted. Desc says tax collected 'until the twelfth century'; article agrees (1161-62 last). Article says Æthelred introduced annual land tax in 1012 and also that 1012 payment was 48,000 pounds: both told. Article gives 'in 1773' for Corn Act-type dating elsewhere; irrelevant.

Article disagrees with itself on the end of the Urbino line: lead says the title was extinguished with Francesco Maria II in 1631 (matches desc), the History section says the dynasty ended 1626 when Urban VIII incorporated Urbino, and the dukes list says the title became extinct with Federico Ubaldo (d. 1623). I gave no year for the incorporation and no year for the end of the title. Left out the unrelated families of the same surname.

Article contradicts itself on who received him: lead says Darius I, exile section says Xerxes I; text says only 'the Persian court'. Article says 'around 491' in lead, '491' in body; desc says 491 deposed; consistent. Left out descendants' link to Nabis (putative).

Article: king from 1075 or 1076 (coronation date disputed); desc says 1076. I gave no year for the coronation. Article doubts that he was ever Ban of Slavonia (desc says earlier ban of Slavonia) and calls him Ban of Croatia from 1070; I wrote only 'ban'. Union with Hungary 1102 from desc not stated in the text I was given, so omitted.

Desc says west bank of the Nile near Qena; article says only 2.5 km south-east of Dendera: not repeated. Desc says begun under Ptolemy XII; article says Ptolemy Auletes (same king), 54 BCE. Article's 'Cleopatra VI' depictions left out. Tourist access sentence omitted ('until November 2025').

Article says secession date disputed; desc says 'mid-3rd century'; I gave both chronologies attributed. Article's lead says independent around 255 BC; I did not print that as fact. Death 'around 235' agrees with desc (3rd century). Parthian invasion c. 250 omitted. Mention of Tarn's daughter hedged by article.

Article lead gives death 343 BC; desc says 'after 344': no death year printed. Article: 'died in the following year in Corinth' omitted. Dionysius II 'under thirty' while dates c. 397 would make him about 30; left as article. Michael Maier's shipwreck legend left out; the teacher at Corinth is from Maier's legend, attributed as 'a tradition'.

Desc says he settled Maroboduus's followers beyond the Danube under Vannius of the Quadi: not in the article, left out. Article: Maroboduus 'fled ... asylum in Rome'. Article gives 'c. 14 BC'; I wrote around 14 BCE. Desc 'reportedly poisoned by Sejanus and his own wife Livilla' attributed to Tacitus and Suetonius.

Desc claims the rift separated Wolaita from neighbours and divided the coast from western highlands in Kenya; the article says nothing of this, so not repeated. Desc says rift runs 'to Mozambique'; article agrees. Left out Hayli Gubbi 2025 eruption and Ol Doinyo Lengai natrocarbonatite details.

Desc mentions a Seljuk army at the 1277 battle and the February 2023 earthquake; article says only 'Mongol army' and nothing of the earthquake, so I wrote only what the article gives. Article says 'mid-10th century' settlement and Armenian settlers. Left out neighbourhood list, notable people and pollution claims.

Article gives death 11 February (lead) and 12 February (body): printed 'February 1680' only. Article says exile 1620 in Netherlands but she was at Heidelberg first; stated as article has it. Philip's duel (1646) and her illness left out.

Article gives Northern pretender 24 May 1382 to 21 October 1392 and legitimate emperor from that date; desc reigned 1382-1412. Text states both as the article does. The article says Go-Kameyama conveyed the regalia, consistent with desc.

Desc orders suppression then curtailment; article has curtailment of principalities provoke the rebellion and then ministers' appointment ended after. Told in the article's order. Article gives death 9 March 141 BC; not printed.

Desc: feng and shan sacrifices at Mount Tai in 1008, Champa rice from Vietnam; article gives no year for Mount Tai and says Champa rice introduced from Champa: I gave no year. Desc says Chanyuan payments of silk and silver; article calls them tribute and gives amounts. The article also says rice seed shipped from Fujian (1011-12) and Champa rice introduced: both stated as the article has them.

Article lead gives his name 'Wu Xian' at other times; left out. Desc says deposed early 684, article 'less than two months' after accession; consistent. Article calls him weak and henpecked in its own voice; I left the judgement out. Dates of the first reign given by desc (end of 683) and article (684): I used 'took the throne' without year.
Desc says rebuilt later; article says Ruri-dō dates to 13th century and the main hall rebuilt 1642. Left out the scroll gallery and walking times.
Article gives Hugh Foot arriving Dec 1956 under a 1957 heading; left out. Article says 'unilateral truce' 1957; omitted. Entry says 'bombings and ambushes'; consistent.
Article calls the Addizione the 'Ercolean Addition'; desc says Addizione Erculea. Boiardo left out of text as in desc. Ariosto added.

Article lead says he served five years; the body says sentenced to fifteen years and released 1924 (desc: fifteen years until 1924). Prison length left out. Article says 'Mühsam did not like cabaret'; omitted. Eicke attribution from 'publications would accuse'.
Article gives 'to 8 November 1918' for reign; entry says abdicated in Nov 1918: consistent. Heading 'Reign' used because he was a reigning duke.
Entry says Duke 'in 1737'; article says elected 1737, invested 1739; both stated. Rundale not mentioned in article's text given (only 'Rastrelli's palace in Mitava'); left out Rundale.

Entry says coalition of five groups formed Oct 1980; article says four in Oct, PRTC joined Dec: wording 'merger of the guerrilla groups, the PRTC joining in December' avoids count. Civil war start: entry 1980, article 1979; not stated.
Article's date of Baur's death (2 Dec 1860) given in lead; not printed. Article contains a long list of scholars' dates for the Clementines; omitted.

Entry says two unsuccessful Bengal invasions and costly Sindh campaign vs Samma; article reports treaty in Bengal and Thatta submission with tribute: outcome of campaigns not labelled success or failure. Article dates Hisar to 1354 and also 'two years after 1353'; omitted. Article says nobles' Khwaja-i-Jahan; kept. Firozabad founding not dated.
Article very thin on history; the 1893 fort and tea in the entry are not in the article, so not repeated. 'seat of the Tooro Kingdom' as article says 'historically'.

Entry: killed 'around 1285'; article: between 1283 and 1286 (and 'died between 1283 and 1286'): used article range, which contains 1285. Boccaccio 27 years after death implies 1286; not printed. Section heading 'Works and ideas' used for her portrayal in Dante; no better heading in the person list.

Entry says died 'a week later' after forced abdication; article says abdication in Oct 1457, 'a week later', yet also deposed 27 Oct and died five days after (1 Nov). Left as 'within days'. Entry's Brescia, Bergamo, Adda not in article; omitted.
Article gives population exceeding 5.9 million; entry says about six million. GDP share and rank omitted as rankings. Entry's Grand Duchy of Hesse link not in article.
Entry says 'supported Sigismund's election as king'; article details this. Entry does not mention Hussites; added. 'Burgrave 1397 to 1427' from lead.

Entry says conquered emirates 1900-1903; article says campaign 1903 secured control. Article's 'Lugard resigned 1906' and 'Governor of Hong Kong from about a year later' (1907) consistent. Left out Dahomey details beyond Nikki.
Article gives 'c. 70 - 26 BC'. Entry says trilingual inscription and Senate condemnation: not in article, omitted. Article attributes the Philae monument to 'erected a monument'. Becker date 1838.
Entry says d. 1364; article gives c. 1290 - c. 1364, 'age of 74'. Kertanegara's death 1292 per inscription. Article says oath 'according to legend'; wrote 'it is said'.

Article calls him 'King of Navarre from 1134'; consistent with entry 1134-1150. 'earned the name the Restorer' is the article's explanation 'election restored independence'. Entry dates c.1112-1150 consistent.

Entry: Sancho II gave Viguera to his brother Ramiro; article calls Ramiro Garcés of Viguera 'first King of Viguera' (d. 981) and says nothing of Sancho granting it; left out. Article's date of Andregoto repudiation 942. Dates consistent with entry 925-970.
Article thin (about 400 words). Entry's Pactolus and Saruhanid beylik not in article; omitted. Ancient section short; word count near lower bound.
Article's 'first Chief of the Prussian General Staff' label not used. Entry says 'trained at Wilhelmstein' consistent.

Entry says seven years of war with Publius; article gives 218-211 BCE (consistent). Article says Gnaeus landed at Emporion with Publius' army sent on; entry says landed at Emporion in 218 (consistent). Article spells the war on the Insubres; entry says nothing of it. Left out Publius's cavalry skirmish at the Rhone.

Entry says 'completed around 1656'; article says construction began early in the reign and halted in 1656 at the sultan's death, with decorative elements unfinished. Text says only that building continued until his death in 1656 and avoids 'completed' or 'unfinished'. Left out tourism, seismic studies, film.

Article gives birth 1509 and death 16 February 1579 and says he died aged 70 (consistent with entry's c. 1509-1579). Article names the Muisca rulers as the psihipqua Bogota (Muyquytá) and the hoa Eucaneme (Hunza); entry speaks of the zipa of Bacata and zaque of Hunza, so rulers are left unnamed. Sun Temple at Sogamoso and the 1538 founding date are not in the article.

SKIPPED: article under 250 words of substance (county facts, a short LAMCO paragraph, lists of people and districts); adds little to the entry Article has no history of Bassa Cove or the colonisation societies, which the entry mentions.

Entry says Madrid Accords 14 November handed territory to Morocco and Mauritania; article agrees. Entry says 'long war with Polisario'; article says 15-year war then ceasefire 1991. Article contains present-day status claims (Spain 2022, AU 2017) which were left out.
Article says he presided over the Red Cross committee and the 1864 conference; entry says co-founder of ICRC (compatible). Left out memorial list and geodetic commission detail.

Article's lead section says expeditions 'between 1869 and 1875' while the journey narrative has him reaching Khartoum in winter 1874; entry says 1869-1874. The text avoids the 1875 end. Entry says he signed protection treaties; the article does not mention treaties, so omitted. Article calls him a military surgeon; entry says physician.

SKIPPED: under 250 words of substance; its History section tells the island of Socotra, not the town, and conflicts in part with the entry (Mahra sultans vs rule of Shihr) Article: 15th century under Shihr; Portuguese 1507 killed the local Mahri ruler; entry says Mahra sultans of Qishn and Socotra ruled 15th century to 1967. Not printed.

SKIPPED: the article is about the present-day Hamburg borough of Harburg (statistics, schools, transport); only three sentences concern the 1927-1937 city, and it says nothing of rubber, oil or port industries Article confirms the 1927 merger and the 1937 Greater Hamburg Act only.
Entry says ruled by Aramaeans, Nabataeans, Romans and Ghassanids; article agrees broadly. Left out the Syrian Civil War and the medieval and Ottoman detail.
Entry says Rostock works 'heavily bombed'; article mentions only a bombing raid on the Rostock factory in early 1942. Not stated heavily. Entry says He 178 flew in 1939 (agrees).

Article gives her wedding as 10 February 1392 (marriage section) and 11 February 1392 (coronation next day, in Life): day left out.
